key_insight: Backward quadrature learning (BQL) learns quadrature for Brownian increments within backward BSDE recursion to solve high-dimensional parametric semilinear parabolic PDEs.
engineering_relevance: BQL can reduce amortized computation when repeatedly evaluating PDE solutions across parameter settings.
method: Learn Brownian-increment quadrature at each time level to approximate local conditional expectations.
Transfer value-function information backward using a continuation surrogate, avoiding nested quadrature.
Derive a global error decomposition and prove first-order mean-square convergence under suitable assumptions.
evidence_signal: On the HJB benchmark across tested dimensions, BQL reports competitive accuracy and approximately 40× and 4× computational cost reductions versus P²INN and FBSNN, respectively, for seven parameter queries.
watch_item: Convergence depends on approximation and integrability assumptions; reported cost gains should not be generalized beyond the tested query workload and benchmarks.
paper_title: Learning the Brownian Motion in Machine Learning for Parametric Parabolic PDEs: A Backward Quadrature Approach
